messages:
Sam K: heads up — eu-west GPU fleet at ~95% usable for the last 45m. tail latency spiked and we've been auto-rejecting a bunch of best-effort calls. I'm proposing we flip admission from immediate-reject -> soft-degrade for non-prod tenants during saturation to reduce 5xx surface. thoughts?

Marta R: can we see the signal breakdown first? is this across all zones or a single AZ? queueing can hide behind "no rejects" but just grow memory usage and increase p99 even more. need limits. @Sam K link to the dashboard? :eyes:

Sam K: single region eu-west-1c mostly, some cross-az spill. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/gpu/usage?region=eu-west-1c — spike started ~2055550700. basically user-facing errors up for low-priority customers.

Ben L: my 2c: prefer a hybrid rule: hard_reject for SLA-backed tenants + queue with bounded wait for mid-tier + soft_degrade for best-effort. soft_degrade = serve via cheaper model variant + prefix-KV reuse when possible. pseudo-config: 

```yaml
admission_policy:
  default: hard_reject
  tiers:
    - name: sla
      mode: hard_reject
    - name: business
      mode: queue
      queue_limit: 200
      max_wait_ms: 250
    - name: best_effort
      mode: soft_degrade
      fallback_model: rwd-small-quant
      degrade_drop_rate: 0.2
```

Ben L: queue_limit here is per-pool, not global. if queue_depth > 2k then abort the soft_degrade experiment.

Dina V: agree with Ben. also add a circuit-breaker that flips back to hard_reject if avg GPU utilization > 97% for 5m or if aggregate queue_latency > 300ms. need clear SLOs so product teams know expected behavior.

Sam K: plan: canary the soft_degrade flow in eu-west-1c for 30m with a 5% traffic slice (non-prod customers only). I'll wire up metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, gpu_util, queue_depth, rejected_count, model_fallback_count.

infra-bot: deployer: canary rollout started by Sam K — admission-policy/v2 -> eu-west-1c (slice=5%). started at 2055554321.

Marta R: ok canary approved with conditions: 1) abort if queue_depth > 500 OR p99 latency increases > 15% vs baseline, 2) notify #incidents and paging rotation, 3) add runaway-protection to autoscaler so it doesn't spin extra cheap nodes that blow cost budget.

Ben L: will apply runtime flags and add metrics export. also will add a debug endpoint to forcibly simulate degrade so QA can validate fallbacks.

Dina V: add a short runbook blurb under /runbooks/fleet-admit so oncall knows what to check. I'll update SLO doc and notify product.

Sam K: thanks all. I'll start canary now and post interim metrics in 10m. :rocket:

Marta R: ack — standing by to abort if thresholds hit. :ok_hand:
